newsitem.title: FRANCE: French centre-right coalition issues manifesto.
newsitem.headline: French centre-right coalition issues manifesto.

text.p: France's ruling centre-right coalition pledged to stabilise public spending, pursue tax cuts and promote negotiations on shorter working hours in an election manifesto issued on Tuesday.

The RPR-UDF platform for a snap May 25-June 1 parliamentary election promised to provide a "new impulse" pledged by President Jacques Chirac by modernising the state, freeing up private initiative, renovating the country's social system and "making France the motor of a citizens' Europe".

Prime Minister Alain Juppe said a re-elected centre-right government would present in its first 40 days a five-year plan for holding the increase in public spending to less than the rate of inflation.
The government would also take an initiative to encourage a flexible approach to shorter working hours through negotiations between employers and trade unions on "chosen working time".

The vaguely-worded manifesto avoided specific commitments on taxes. It said the coalition would "accentuate the reduction of social welfare charges on lower salaries in exchange for the creation of jobs...continue the reduction of income tax and launch a reform of the professional (business) tax".
The only apparent new spending pledge was to raise the maximum age for the payment of child benefit, without saying by how much.
